input.quote: 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the Fees paid or payable by Customer under the first Order Form during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.
input.rationale: Section 21 is mutual and carries the full preferred carve-out set (confidentiality, data protection/security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement) plus a mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages. The cap basis, however, is illusory and fails even the fallback: "Fees" is defined (1.5/1.6) as only the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee stated in the first Order Form, and the cap is further limited to the first Order Form, so both Parties' aggregate liability is effectively USD 12,000 — far below 6 months' fees (walk-away). The payment carve-out in 21.3 is tied to the same narrow "Fees" noun, so Customer's real payment obligations are not excluded from capped damages. We therefore make two surgical edits: restate the cap as the greater of lowercase fees paid or payable under this Agreement and all Order Forms in the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000 (retaining the existing temporal anchor), and change the payment carve-out to "amounts due". All other elements are already met and are left untouched.

proposal.summary: Fix illusory cap basis (narrow "Fees" = USD 12,000 implementation fee under the first Order Form) and broaden the payment carve-out.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] "Fees" is defined as only the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form, so the mutual cap is illusory; we set it at the greater of lowercase fees paid or payable in the twelve months preceding the event and USD 1,000,000, and we conform the payment carve-out to all amounts due so Customer's payment obligations are not treated as capped damages. Indemnities, confidentiality, data protection and security remain outside the cap as Excluded Claims.
